I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou County, that is the system I trust most because it fits our climate, fits my labor, and gives me the most stable grain output and income across the whole year. I will harvest the winter wheat first, then plant summer maize right after, using the same fields without leaving them idle. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is steady and easier to manage, and hybrid seed for maize because I want stronger yield in summer. I will not spread my land across too many crops, because that makes fieldwork, fertilizer use, irrigation, and pest control harder for me to manage. I will plough before the wheat season to set up a clean seedbed, then use rotary tillage after wheat harvest so I can plant maize quickly. I will apply moderate fertilizer, irrigate wheat more than maize, and keep pesticide use limited to the times I think pressure is high enough to justify the cost.
